acceptanceCriteria.description: Invocation, catalog, protected-context, and guard ports expose only provider-neutral safe types, require explicit approved-source associations, and remain free of outer-layer imports.

Protected context validation enforces exact structural associations, bounded content/history/settings, rejects unsafe structured or high-confidence secret payloads, and permits legitimate technical discussion.

The Prompt 5 orchestrator reuses Prompt 4 approval validity, orders adapter/runtime/context checks correctly, maps safe outcomes, invokes once only on success, and contains no persistence or logging behavior.

Committed conflict markers and stale Prompt 5-only status claims are removed, later adapter/lifecycle consumers remain compatible, and applicable focused, documentation, architecture, agent-support, build, and non-browser gates pass.

risks: Strengthening port signatures affects the later Python adapter, Prompt 7 submit use case, read-model availability, and shared host composition.

The current host context seam has no approved asset-backed instruction materializer; the Prompt 5 repair must require source association and keep instruction materialization behind the port without fabricating prompt text.

research.summary: The current branch proves Prompt 4 eligibility and approval through application use cases and repository-backed invocation-time revalidation. Prompt 5 ports and services are application-local, but the port family lacks structured source associations, selection/guard validation is pass-through, context validation has conflicting implementations, and the orchestrator has committed conflict markers. The shared host currently materializes only the user message while the later Python adapter and persisted lifecycle consumers already exist. The repair should strengthen the Prompt 5 seam and make context/source association explicit without inventing provider, persistence, or UI behavior.
